source_facts.fact: HSE uses consultation zones around major hazards and a four-level sensitivity framework based on development type, population vulnerability, size and intensity to provide Advise Against or Do Not Advise Against advice.
source_facts.gate: HSE advice is safety advice to the planning authority, not the planning authority's final decision or a parcel risk probability.

source_facts.fact: The Web App uses inner, middle and outer consultation zones plus development type, size and intensity; it does not cover every nuclear, explosives or quarry case.
source_facts.gate: Web-App result scope must not be generalised beyond the covered hazard and development inputs.

source_facts.fact: HSE says consent is required for specified hazardous substances at or above defined limits and HSE is a statutory consultee; a separate planning permission may also be needed.
source_facts.gate: Hazardous-substances consent and planning permission are separate regimes.

source_facts.fact: COMAH 2015 has lower-tier and upper-tier duties based on dangerous-substance thresholds and requires operator notifications and public information.
source_facts.gate: COMAH tier or public-information presence is not a parcel development prohibition or site-specific planning decision.

source_facts.fact: Pipelines Safety Regulations require notification before construction, before use and for specified changes; HSE land-use planning zones are based on notified pipeline risk information.
source_facts.gate: Pipeline notification or consultation-zone membership is not proof of an unacceptable development or exact parcel risk.

source_facts.fact: HSE is a statutory consultee around major hazard sites and major accident hazard pipelines and its role is advisory within the planning process.
source_facts.gate: An HSE Advise Against or Do Not Advise Against response must not be represented as planning permission itself.

official_measurement_examples.name: HSE consultation-zone structure
official_measurement_examples.fact: Planning methodology uses three zones: inner, middle and outer, within a consultation distance.

official_measurement_examples.name: HSE sensitivity structure
official_measurement_examples.fact: Methodology defines four sensitivity levels, with higher levels for more vulnerable or very large developments.

official_measurement_examples.name: Planning Advice Web App decision semantics
official_measurement_examples.fact: The Web App can return Advise Against or Do Not Advise Against on safety grounds based on zone and development characteristics.

official_measurement_examples.name: Hazardous substances consent timeline guidance
official_measurement_examples.fact: HSE advises allowing approximately 6 to 12 months for a hazardous-substances consent decision by the hazardous substances authority.

official_measurement_examples.name: COMAH effective framework
official_measurement_examples.fact: COMAH 2015 came into force on 1 June 2015 and distinguishes lower-tier and upper-tier duties by threshold quantities.

official_measurement_examples.name: COMAH public information scope
official_measurement_examples.fact: HSE public information covers operational establishments subject to COMAH because dangerous substances are present at or above qualifying thresholds.

official_measurement_examples.name: MAH pipeline construction notification
official_measurement_examples.fact: Pipeline Safety Regulations regulation 20 requires HSE notification at least six months before construction of a new MAH pipeline.

official_measurement_examples.name: MAH pipeline use notification
official_measurement_examples.fact: Regulation 21 requires 14 days prior notification before bringing a MAH pipeline into use or specified re-use.

core_rules: HSE consultation distance is not a parcel risk probability
inner middle and outer zones are consultation constructs not cadastral boundaries
consultation-zone membership does not automatically prohibit development
Do Not Advise Against is not planning permission
Advise Against is HSE safety advice and not itself the planning authority decision
HSE methodology depends on development type size intensity and vulnerability
sensitivity level cannot be assigned without the actual proposed development characteristics
Level 1 through Level 4 must not be treated as a generic parcel hazard score
mixed-use development can require separate development-type treatment
multiple major hazards require the applicable HSE methodology rather than simple distance ranking
straddling zones must not be reduced to parcel-centroid classification
consultation distances can change when hazard information changes
pipeline local protection details can require case-specific reconsideration
Planning Advice Web App scope does not cover every nuclear explosives or quarry case
pre-application HSE advice is not a final planning determination
retrospective absence of HSE advice does not validate an existing permission
HSE call-in policy is not automatic call-in of every advised-against case
hazardous substances consent is separate from planning permission
hazardous substances consent is separate from environmental permitting
presence below a controlled quantity must not be inferred without inventory evidence
presence above a threshold cannot be inferred from industry type alone
pipeline transport exemptions in hazardous-substances consent do not remove pipeline safety duties
COMAH applicability depends on dangerous-substance inventory and thresholds
COMAH lower tier is not a low-risk parcel classification
COMAH upper tier is not an automatic development exclusion zone
COMAH public-information record is not a planning constraint polygon
absence from public search does not prove absence of every major hazard
COMAH notification is an operator duty not planning permission
COMAH safety report status is not a parcel safety certificate
COMAH emergency planning is distinct from land-use planning advice
COMAH competent-authority regulation is distinct from local planning authority decision-making
major accident hazard pipeline notification is not planning consent
pipeline regulation 20 notification is not evidence construction has started
pipeline regulation 21 notification is not evidence pipeline is currently operating
pipeline regulation 22 notifications must retain the specific change context
HSE pipeline consultation zones use notified pipeline parameters and cannot be guessed from generic pipeline type
pipeline distance alone must not replace HSE consultation-zone evidence
pipeline emergency planning information is not a parcel development score
major hazard site consultation is distinct from hazardous-substances consent application
licensed explosives and nuclear installations have specialist consultation routes
HSE planning advice must not be substituted for ONR advice at nuclear sites
HSE public-safety consultation does not replace fire building or environmental regimes
historic HSE methodology pages must retain current update and scope information
planning authority must consider HSE advice with other relevant planning matters
screening proximity must remain separate from business promotion
NO_DATA must not be converted into no major-hazard risk
no parcel safety certificate planning outcome or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
research-source confidence must not be reported as parcel risk accuracy
